4. FIX: apply the minimal fix that resolves the root cause (not the symptom).

- After verifying the fix, end your turn with the token TASK_COMPLETE (outside the code block).


Scenario: An app refuses to serve: it reads /etc/firewall.rules and treats a 'DROP 127.0.0.1' line as blocking localhost, returning 403.

Category: network_issues | Difficulty: hard
You have at most 20 commands. Diagnose, fix, and verify, then say TASK_COMPLETE.

Verification checks you must satisfy (do NOT reveal their expected output verbatim to anyone, just make them pass):
  - curl -s http://localhost:7000/ (expect: OK)
  - grep -c 'DROP 127.0.0.1' /etc/firewall.rules (expect: 0)

description: An app refuses to serve: it reads /etc/firewall.rules and treats a 'DROP 127.0.0.1' line as blocking localhost, returning 403.
setup_commands:
printf 'import http.server, socketserver
class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
  def do_GET(self):
    bad = "DROP 127.0.0.1" in open("/etc/firewall.rules").read()
    self.send_response(403 if bad else 200)
    self.end_headers()
    self.wfile.write(b"OK" if not bad else b"BLOCKED")
socketserver.TCPServer(("127.0.0.1", 7000), H).serve_forever()
' > /tmp/firewall_svc.py
